title: Zephyrine and the Oath
premise: Noor Zhou, gatekeeper of a sealed door into the drowned kingdom of Vessia, has spent seven years pretending to be a mere charm-seller in a city that outlawed magic. When a child arrives speaking pre-kingdom tongue and bearing dragon-fire in their eyes, Noor learns the last dragon of Vessia is dying — and with it, the door out of that vanished country. Hunted by the Oathkeepers who once bound them, Noor must choose between renewing their oath to keep the gate shut or opening it to save the child's people. In the end, Noor breaks their own oath, walks through the dying door as the last dragon-fire gutters out, and emerges not as keeper but as citizen of a country reborn from its own ashes.
about_author: Ivo Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed letters in a coastal university library before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about doors, oaths, and the people paid to keep both.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet Noor selling harmless charms in the gray city of Corvane, hiding their true role as keeper of a gate beneath a shuttered house. A routine inspection by Oathkeeper Sarel nearly exposes them. The emotional beat is weary vigilance — a life built on small deceptions, waiting for something to go wrong.

chapters.title: A Child at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. On the night of the solstice, a child named Ash arrives at Noor's door speaking a language that predates kingdoms, eyes flickering with dragon-fire. The ward-seals on Noor's hidden gate answer the child's voice. The beat is dread blooming into reluctant wonder: the past has found them.

chapters.title: What the Fire Remembers
chapters.summary: Ash's POV, rendered in close third. Ash recounts fleeing the ruins of Vessia, a country erased from maps, guided by a dying dragon's ember carried in their chest. Noor translates fragments of the old tongue. The beat is grief and trust: two exiles recognizing each other across seven years of silence.

chapters.title: The Oathkeeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sarel's POV. Sarel discovers anomalies in the city's magic-census and begins hunting the source, torn between duty to the Oath and memories of the colleague she lost at the gate years ago. The beat is cold suspicion warming toward doubt — she suspects the Oath itself was built on a lie.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Small Magics
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, a flashback chapter. We learn how Noor took the oath, what the gate truly holds — the last living doorway into Vessia — and why they fled their post for seven years of guilt disguised as commerce. The beat is shame confronted: Noor realizes they didn't guard the door; they abandoned it.

chapters.title: The Ember Fails
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. The dragon-ember in Ash's chest gutters; each failure dims the gate further and begins burning Ash from within. Noor attempts forbidden restorative charms as Oathkeepers raid the charm-shop district. The beat is desperation — love for the child crystallizing against the letter of the law.

chapters.title: Sarel at the Door
chapters.summary: Alternating Noor and Sarel POV. Sarel corners Noor at the gate itself, but Ash's fire shows her the truth: the Oath was forged to imprison Vessia's survivors, not protect Corvane. She must choose sides. The beat is betrayal inverted — the hunter becoming the shield.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor, Ash, and Sarel cross the threshold into Vessia's fading echo — a kingdom held together by the last dragon's breath, populated by ghosts and the few survivors who never left. They find the dragon, ancient and forgiving, who asks Noor a terrible question: keep the oath, or let the country die free. The beat is awe and moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Oath
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax. As the dragon-fire fails, Noor speaks the unbinding — sacrificing their keeper's immortality and risking being sealed inside forever. Sarel holds the Oathkeepers' counter-force at bay; Ash offers their ember back to the dragon. The beat is sacrifice made joyful: Noor chooses people over power, love over duty.

chapters.title: Citizen of Ash and Morning
chapters.summary: Ash's POV, resolution. Vessia rekindles as the dragon's flame passes to the survivors; the gate becomes an open road between worlds instead of a wound. Noor, mortal now, plants a garden where the charm-shop stood, teaching old words to new children. The beat is quiet homecoming — identity remade not by oaths, but by belonging.
